title: XProtect Malware Detection
description: Apple's XProtect detected a known-malicious file. Fires only when Apple's own signatures match, so a hit is high-confidence and always worth reviewing.
author: so-crates

title: Endpoint Security Client Loaded (Kernel Extension)
description: A kernel extension was loaded. Modern macOS heavily restricts kexts and legitimate loads on a user Mac are rare; malicious ones typically load rootkit or driver components.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: Kext-based drivers installed by the user

title: Background Task Management: Persistence Item Added
description: A LaunchAgent, LaunchDaemon, or login item was registered with Background Task Management. Every persistence vector on modern macOS passes through this event.
author: so-crates

title: BTM Persistence Added Under User Library
description: A user-scope LaunchAgent was registered. Distinct from the general BTM rule because per-user LaunchAgents are the single most common macOS malware persistence technique.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'btm_launch_item_add' AND (LaunchItemPath LIKE '%/Library/LaunchAgents/%' ESCAPE '\' OR LaunchItemPath LIKE '%/Library/LaunchDaemons/%' ESCAPE '\')

title: TCC Permission Modified
description: An app's Transparency, Consent, and Control permissions were changed (grant or revoke). Malware routinely tampers with TCC to gain access to microphone, camera, screen recording, or Full Disk Access.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: User approving a legitimate app permission

title: TCC Modification: High-Value Permission
description: Full Disk Access, Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Accessibility permissions were modified. These are the specific TCC rights sought by macOS surveillance tooling.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: User consent dialogs from a legitimate app
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'tcc_modify' AND (TccService LIKE '%SystemPolicyAllFiles%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%ScreenCapture%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%Microphone%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%Camera%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%Accessibility%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%PostEvent%' ESCAPE '\' OR TccService LIKE '%ListenEvent%' ESCAPE '\')

title: Gatekeeper User Override
description: The user forcibly ran a file Gatekeeper wanted to block (Control-click open, or `spctl --add`). Legitimate developers do this on their own tools; on an ordinary user Mac it typically follows a social-engineering step.
author: so-crates

title: Remote Thread Created in Another Process
description: A process created a new thread inside a different process's address space (process injection via task_for_pid + thread_create). The primitive is documented but rare in legitimate software.
author: so-crates

title: Code Signature Invalidated at Runtime
description: A running process had its code signing status invalidated. This is what happens when code is injected or the binary on disk is tampered with while it runs; benign programs almost never trigger it.
author: so-crates

title: SSH Login Success
description: An interactive SSH session opened. Informational on Macs that expect SSH; investigable when Remote Login isn't supposed to be on.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'openssh_login' AND Success = 1

title: SSH Login Failure
description: SSH authentication failed. A single failure is noise; a burst from the same source address is a brute-force pattern.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'openssh_login' AND Success = 0

title: Screen Sharing Session Opened
description: An inbound Screen Sharing / Apple Remote Desktop session attached. Investigable when unexpected; scam-callers routinely convince targets to enable and connect to this.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'screensharing_attach' AND Success = 1

title: Configuration Profile Installed
description: A configuration profile was installed. Profiles can enroll a Mac in MDM, install root CAs, or force VPN routing; malicious profile installs are the standard adware/spyware persistence.
author: so-crates

title: Local User Created via Open Directory
description: A new local account was created through Open Directory (dscl, sysadminctl, System Settings). A backdoor account is the classic post-exploitation persistence move.
author: so-crates

title: User Added to Admin Group
description: A user was added to the local admin group, granting sudo without further authentication. Post-exploitation privilege escalation via directory service tampering.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: Legitimate promotion of a standard user by an admin
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'od_group_add' AND GroupName = 'admin'

title: Disk Image or Volume Mounted
description: A file system was mounted. Informational; useful chained with any exec that follows out of the mounted path.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: Ordinary DMG opens and USB drive plug-ins

title: Sudo Command Executed
description: A sudo command ran. Informational on interactive Macs; unexpected sudo from a non-terminal parent is more meaningful.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'sudo' AND Success = 1

title: Sudo Command Denied
description: A sudo attempt was rejected. A single denial is a typo; a cluster is a probe against the sudoers policy.
author: so-crates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'sudo' AND Success = 0

title: su to Root Success
description: Someone su'd to root and it worked. Rare on modern Macs since root is disabled by default and sudo is preferred; a success here means root was explicitly enabled first.
author: so-crates
falsepositives: Admin who has deliberately enabled the root account
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE EventType = 'su' AND Success = 1 AND TargetUsername = 'root'

title: Password Modified via Open Directory
description: A local account's password was changed through Open Directory. Ordinary when the user resets their own; investigable when it changes an account other than the one performing the action.
author: so-crates
